name: Delaware

sales.rateNote: Delaware has no sales tax at the state or local level. Instead, sellers pay a gross receipts tax (a business license tax on their receipts, not itemized to buyers), e.g. 0.7468% for general retailers after a $100,000 monthly deduction.

local.levies: none: no city or county sales tax

groceries.note: No sales tax. Grocery supermarkets pay a 0.3267% gross receipts tax on their receipts.

clothing.note: No sales tax on any retail purchase.

otherRates.note: Paid at titling: $5.25 per $100 of purchase price above $500 ($8 under $400; $13.75 from $400 to $500).

otherRates.item: hotel, motel and tourist home rooms
otherRates.note: 8% tax collected from the guest and remitted to the Division of Revenue.

otherRates.item: lessee use of tangible personal property (leases)
otherRates.note: Lessee use tax rate on leased goods and leased motor vehicles.

sales.holidayNote: No sales tax, so no sales tax holiday.

useTax.note: No general consumer use tax. A lessee use tax of 1.9914% applies to leases of tangible personal property.

facts.text: Delaware has no state or local sales tax; businesses pay a gross receipts tax instead.
General retailers pay a 0.7468% gross receipts tax, after a $100,000 deduction per month for the whole enterprise (30 Del. C. ch. 29).
Gross receipts tax rates vary by business type: 0.3267% for grocery supermarkets, 0.6472% for restaurants and contractors, 0.3983% for services and wholesalers, 0.0945% to 0.1260% for manufacturers.
Buying a car in Delaware costs a 5.25% document fee ($5.25 per $100 of price) instead of a sales tax.
Hotel and motel rooms carry an 8% state lodging tax paid by the guest.

property.levied: Local: the three counties (New Castle, Kent, Sussex), municipalities and school districts levy real property taxes; school district taxes are the largest part. There is no state property tax.

assessment.text: Real property is assessed at fair market value as of the county's most recent reassessment base year (9 Del. C. 8306); each county must reassess at least once every 5 years from the date its general reassessment is certified.

homestead.name: Senior School Property Tax Credit
homestead.text: Homeowners aged 65+ get a credit against school district property tax on their principal residence equal to the lesser of 50% of the school tax or $500. Those who moved to Delaware after 2017 need 10 consecutive years of domicile (3 years for 2013-2017 arrivals). There is no general homestead exemption for all owners.
homestead.applyBy: Apply to the county receiver of taxes or treasurer by April 30 before the tax year.

facts.text: Every county must reassess all real property at least once every 5 years, counted from the certification of its last general reassessment.
After a general reassessment, school boards must reset tax rates so that revenue does not exceed the prior year's operating revenue plus allowed growth.
School districts entirely in New Castle County may set a higher nonresidential rate, up to 1.85 times the residential rate.
The senior school tax credit is withdrawn the following year if the property tax bill is not paid in full.
Kent and Sussex Boards of Assessment Review hear appeals from March 1 to May 31.

uncertain: Property tax due dates differ by county (and some municipalities bill separately); no statewide due date, left null.
Dates of each county's most recent general reassessment (base year) were not read on county sites.
